note: Chat Completions publishes no version header at all, so the date is the whole identity. OpenRouter adds vendor extensions on top of the OpenAI contract, and the rows below are those, read from the real arm captures in testdata/provider/openrouter. The request leg rows come from the harness shapes added 2026-10-03 (router-infra#90), which are derived from each harness's request builder rather than captured on the wire. reasoning_details is no longer a row on the response or stream leg: since #90 the wire structs name it, and it is carried as an opaque member of the reasoning content (reasoning_details.go). native_finish_reason is no longer a row either: both wire structs name it, because a native length reason makes a tool call cut at the output limit a length stop. The stream leg repeats most of the response leg because a streamed response is decoded through chatChunkWire and a non-streamed one through chatResponseWire: production prunes each against its own struct, so a row on one says nothing about the other. Every row drops on every target: an unmodelled provider member is pruned before decode, so it reaches no client, not even a Chat client.

OpenRouter's own billing figure. The Router reads it best-effort into its usage record as the provider-reported charge, beside its own rate-card price; a value that is not a number is left unknown, never a decode failure. No codec publishes it, so a client never sees two disagreeing numbers.
Read best-effort as a raw member: only upstream_inference_cost is taken, into the usage record. The per-direction splits beside it are ignored, not pruned. No codec publishes it.
Decoded into the usage record: on a BYOK call usage.cost is OpenRouter's fee alone. No codec publishes it.
